title: Photo Sharing (Flickr / Google Photos)
summary: Build a personal photo library with resumable uploads, album sharing, asynchronous thumbnails and fast CDN reads.
narrative:
Build a Flickr / Google Photos-style library: users upload photos resumably, organise albums, share albums by link, browse a timeline, and search by date or place. Unlike Instagram (level-14), there is no follower feed. The APIs are POST /uploads to create a resumable session, PUT chunks to that session, POST /photos to commit, GET /photos/{id}?size= to select a rendition, GET /albums/{id}, and POST /albums/{id}/share. Authorise private albums and issue scoped CDN links for photo reads; sharing links grant access only to their intended album.

The hard parts are storing billions of small files and serving them quickly. Haystack avoids multiple filesystem-metadata seeks per photo by packing photos into large append-only volume files and locating them through an in-memory index of volume ids and offsets. Blob Storage plays that photo store here. NoSQL holds owner, album membership, volume/offset per size, EXIF date/place and content hash for deduplication; date/place access paths also support basic library searches. Expect ~100 M uploads/day ≈ 1.2 K/s, with ~5× holiday peaks. At ~3 MB/original, originals add ~300 TB/day; four thumbnails totaling ~150 KB add ~15 TB/day. Reads are ~10× uploads and skew toward recent photos.

Clients use a Load Balancer and redundant Web Servers for uploads and metadata, and a CDN backed by Blob Storage for photo bytes. Cache hot metadata and commit the original durably before publishing a photo-uploaded event to a Message Queue. Redundant Workers generate four thumbnail sizes asynchronously, write the renditions to Blob Storage and mark each size ready in NoSQL with idempotent updates; return a pending rendition state until ready. The CDN absorbs hot reads so the photo store mainly serves misses and the long tail. Optionally have Workers populate a Search Index for richer date/place and available detected-label searches, and add Monitoring for upload failures and thumbnail backlog.

functional: Create resumable upload sessions, accept chunks and commit photos with durable originals
Organise albums, create sharing links, browse a timeline and search by date/place
Store photo and album metadata, per-size blob locations, EXIF date/place and dedupe hashes in NoSQL
Serve photo bytes through CDN → Blob Storage and cache hot metadata at the app tier
Enqueue committed uploads; generate four thumbnail sizes in Workers and mark sizes ready in NoSQL
nonFunctional: Handle ~1.2 K uploads/s on average with ~5× peaks and ~10× as many reads
Survive one Web Server or Worker failure
Keep thumbnail work off upload requests and make retries idempotent
constraints: Never connect Web Server directly to Worker; thumbnail work must be queued
Clients must not access NoSQL directly; authorise metadata and album operations at the app tier
Connect Blob Storage to the CDN for photo reads; enforce private/shared album access on CDN delivery
Keep blob bytes in the photo store and point-lookups or readiness updates in NoSQL
capacity: Four thumbnails total ~150 KB/photo → ~15 TB/day; reads ~10× uploads
specs.tradeoff: Packing small photos into append-only volumes reduces metadata seeks but complicates deletion and compaction; Blob Storage represents that durable photo-store abstraction. Asynchronous renditions shorten upload handling while introducing a readiness delay, and CDN caching reduces origin load while requiring careful access control.
specs.bonus: Connect Workers to Search Index for richer date/place and detected-label search when labels are available, and add Monitoring for upload and rendition failures.

missions.label: Fetch photo bytes from Blob Storage

topologyRules.message: Don't generate thumbnails inline in the upload request — enqueue them
Clients access photo and album metadata through the Web Server API.

resilienceRules.message: Run at least two Web Servers so uploads and album browsing survive one failure.
Run at least two Workers so a failure does not stop thumbnail generation.
Connect Blob Storage to the CDN so photo reads can be served near users.

hints: Start with Client → CDN → Blob Storage for photos and Client → Load Balancer → Web Server for APIs. Connect Web Server to Blob Storage for originals, NoSQL for photo/album metadata, and Cache for hot metadata.

Connect Web Server → Message Queue → Worker. The Worker writes thumbnails to Blob Storage and marks sizes ready in NoSQL. Keep generation asynchronous and use repeatable rendition keys so retries do not create duplicate sizes.

Run two Web Servers and two Workers. Each Web Server connects to Blob Storage, NoSQL, Cache and Message Queue; the queue feeds both Workers, each writing Blob Storage and NoSQL. Add Worker → Search Index and Web Server → Monitoring; retain CDN → Blob Storage.
